notes.text: Jared Spurgeon is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes. That pair has had 37% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 87:34 together, down from 69% with Spurgeon.

Brock Faber is on injured reserve (skull surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 193:00 together.
Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (ankle injury) and has missed the last 15 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Josh Anderson is away for personal reasons and missed their last game.

Mike Matheson is out two weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 70:40 together, up from 41% with Matheson.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Wild go in first in the Central with 28 points, the Canadiens second in the Atlantic with 25 points.

MTL.head: Close, but the Wild have the slight edge
MTL.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Canadiens’ best way to tip it is piling up shots.

MIN.head: Leaning the Wild’s way
MIN.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents lately. Still, it’s close: the Canadiens can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: A heavyweight meeting
paras: The Canadiens have won two in a row, while the Wild (12-3-4) lost 4-3 in overtime to Tampa Bay on Saturday. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (third in the NHL) and the Habs second in the Atlantic (seventh).

The Wild’s record (.737) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.655), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Canadiens’ (.735 on chances worth .561), largely because they’re 7-4 in one-goal games.

The Wild let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (3rd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). The Canadiens, by contrast, take more penalties than they draw (31st). Minnesota has allowed 2.26 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th). Something has to give when the Wild’s shooting runs into the Canadiens’ defense. On top of that, the Wild keep dangerous shots away, but the Canadiens give up a lot of them.

Kirill Kaprizov (16 G / 15 A / 31 P in 19 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is tied for third in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Montréal. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 20 A / 26 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind, with eight points in his last five games. For the Canadiens, Lane Hutson (3 G / 14 A / 17 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Cole Caufield (11 G / 5 A / 16 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL.

Jesper Wallstedt (11-2-3 / .922 SV% in 16 GS) has been terrific for Minnesota and will likely start. Montréal has two options in net: Jacob Fowler (8-1-1 / .925 SV% in 10 GS) and Jakub Dobeš (3-2-2 / .846 SV% in 7 GS). Fowler has started seven of their last ten games, including the last one on Saturday, so Montréal could turn to Dobeš to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: The Wild have been without Jared Spurgeon since Oct 27, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Canadiens are newly without Josh Anderson, and have been without Ivan Demidov, Samuel Montembeault and Mike Matheson for several games.
Joel Eriksson Ek has five goals on chances worth about 10.0 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Kirill Kaprizov, Quinn Hughes and Joel Eriksson Ek have a point in eight straight games.
